newsitem.title: USA: CSX optimistic on possibility of Norfolk talks. [Corrected 01:02 GMT 24/1]
newsitem.headline: CSX optimistic on possibility of Norfolk talks. [Corrected 01:02 GMT 24/1]

text.p: CSX Corp Chairman John Snow, after a telephone conversation with David Goode, chairman of Norfolk Southern Corp, said he was optimistic about the possibility of a meeting between the rival railroad companies.

Speaking at an earnings presentation on Thursday in New York, Snow said, "I had a very cordial and friendly conversation with David Goode. It suggested to me he's as anxious as we are to meet and carry on conversations."
No date has been set yet for a meeting, he said.

The companies have been locked in a three-month takeover battle for Conrail Inc. Norfolk Southern is trying to block a proposed merger between CSX and Conrail and buy Philadelphia based-Conrail itself.

CSX officials also said it had capitalized its 1996 costs related to the proposed merger. They called the costs "fairly modest" but declined to give specific numbers. In response to a question, one official said the costs were "well less than $100 million."

"We have in mind granting Norfolk Southern access whether by ownership or trackage, etc., ... to give them a competitive system while sustaining as many of the benefits as possible" from the proposed Conrail merger, Snow said.

CSX (corrects source) also said it expected revenues in its transportation business to grow about three percent in 1997, or by about $140 million to $145 million. It expects about 80 to 84 percent of the increase to add to its bottom line.
